bug_semantics: The Git node accepted an attacker-selected local repository and ran push/pushTags while Git's file transport remained permitted. An authenticated workflow author could stage repository metadata whose configured local target was a crafted repository containing receive hooks; the local git-receive-pack path then executed those hooks as the n8n process. The later default core.hooksPath=/dev/null mitigation covered hooks for the invoking repository but did not make a write to an attacker-controlled local target safe. The fix validates configured remotes and, when hooks are disabled, removes file from GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL specifically for push and pushTags.
flaw_origin: The first Git node implementation trusted repository-controlled local configuration and destination selection: it constructed simple-git with a workflow-supplied baseDirectory and exposed git.push() without restricting local remote targets or the file transport. This crossed a trust boundary from an authenticated workflow into Git's executable receive-hook behavior.
ai_marker: absent: the BIC commit object identifies author and committer Jan Oberhauser <jan.oberhauser@gmail.com>, has the exact message ':sparkles: Add Git-Node', contains no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with trailer, and neither identity is a bot
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/security/advisories/GHSA-rcv6-pvrj-4xcg describes authenticated RCE from a staged crafted local repository and fixes 1.123.67, 2.31.5, and 2.32.1. `git log --follow --reverse -- packages/nodes-base/nodes/Git/Git.node.ts` finds the public landing squash 3667b0dd01f82046549b795b98b88983bd7c7fbb ('Add Git node', PR #1820); `git log -L 543,551:packages/nodes-base/nodes/Git/Git.node.ts` traces the relevant Git invocation/protocol lineage from that landing through 46c1a0e8f32db71c79ec4187f75d2184053f1dad and the fix 2222fe3a6c886a9059f28e1b6d4bdb10ee420624. The first-party PR commits API https://api.github.com/repos/n8n-io/n8n/pulls/1820/commits?per_page=100 decomposes the squash: its first member f81e76aca958dab7392942e8a74b7919e7db42b5 creates packages/nodes-base/nodes/Git/Git.node.ts, accepts workflow parameter baseDirectory, passes it as simpleGit({baseDir}), and exposes `await git.push()` without protocol/local-target restriction. The commit API reports parent 06dd4236482d345b1193b87b993c944b117698bd and the file status `added`; a direct Contents API lookup of that same path at the parent returns HTTP 404, proving immediate-parent absence. The squash landing diff also reports the Git node file as newly created. `git tag --contains 3667b0dd01f82046549b795b98b88983bd7c7fbb --list 'n8n@*' | sort -V` starts at n8n@0.123.0, well before every advisory upper bound. Public fix PR #34680 decomposes to direct member 97f5ba3f824019665adb81a9976174e5f778d71d, whose Git.node.ts patch adds `isWriteOperation` and changes GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL from `file:git:http:https:ssh` to `git:http:https:ssh` for push/pushTags when hooks are disabled, plus configured-remote validation; squash landing 2222fe3a6c886a9059f28e1b6d4bdb10ee420624 carries it to public history. Equivalent backports are 1cd2c5fb22a906058cc083c3af2d561ce7f4332d (1.x), f6cb6cf3ab177c3740a5ef624b89bae5165405a1 (2.31.x), and f69dfc6dd2178a14ea1624d2e1d403c2e755042f (2.32.x). `git tag --contains` starts those branches at n8n@1.123.67, n8n@2.31.5, and n8n@2.32.1 respectively, and direct diffs from 1.123.66/2.31.4/2.32.0 to those patched tags show the file-transport restriction appearing exactly at the stated boundaries.
reasoning: The vulnerability is in the Git node's original trust model, not in a later move or refactor. The staged repository controls Git remote metadata; push to a local crafted target enters Git's receive side and can run target hooks in the n8n process. Later path checks and core.hooksPath hardening narrowed other routes but left this local write transport reachable, so they do not replace the original BIC. The main-history commit 3667b0dd01f82046549b795b98b88983bd7c7fbb is a squash aggregate, and treating it as the BIC would violate the protocol because PR #1820's retained commit objects reconstruct the smaller member. Member f81e76aca958dab7392942e8a74b7919e7db42b5 is the earliest member and already contains both causal ingredients: attacker-selected local baseDirectory and unrestricted `git.push()`. Its immediate parent lacks the Git node path, while later members merely expand operations (for example pushTags) or refine the node. The patch lifecycle and exact tag boundaries corroborate this mechanism: the decisive remediation disables local file transport for write operations when hooks are not enabled. AI attribution is therefore judged only on f81e76aca958dab7392942e8a74b7919e7db42b5; its commit object is human-authored/committed and has no AI trailer. AI/bot markers on the 2026 fix bundles are irrelevant to BIC attribution, yielding NOT_AI.
